title: DGGI Patna Zonal Unit unearths GST refund fraud exceeding ₹88 crore in tobacco sector; Cigarettes valued at over ₹150 crore placed under prohibition
body_text: Continuing its sustained efforts to curb tax evasion in the tobacco sector, the Patna Zonal Unit of Directorate General of GST Intelligence (DGGI) has unearthed a syndicate engaged in fraudulent availment of GST refunds. Investigation has revealed that the syndicate was operating through a network of shell entities that procured invoices from dealers of branded cigarettes without actual receipt of the underlying goods, thereby fraudulently availing substantial amounts of Input Tax Credit (ITC) in violation of Section 16 of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017. The syndicate was also procuring substandard cigarettes of unknown origin and supplying the same to Falta Special Economic Zone (SEZ), Kolkata, under Letter of Undertaking (LUT). Subsequently, fraudulent GST refund claims were made against the accumulated input tax credit on account of such deemed exports. Investigation has revealed that the syndicate obtained refunds exceeding ₹ 88 crore during the last two years by adopting the aforesaid modus operandi . During the course of the investigation, approximately 8.76 crore sticks (8,410 cartons) of suspected counterfeit and substandard cigarettes bearing the names of various reputed brands, having an aggregate MRP value exceeding ₹ 150 crore , were found at Falta SEZ, Kolkata, and were placed under prohibition. Further investigation is in progress to identify the entities and persons involved in the syndicate and the full quantum of tax evasion and fraudulent refunds. DGGI has cracked down heavily on syndicates involved in illegal manufacture, clandestine supply, passing on of ineligible Input Tax Credit (ITC), diversion of branded cigarettes through cash transactions, and export/ supply to SEZs of substandard cigarettes mis-declared as branded cigarettes. In the months of September and October this year, two illicit cigarette manufacturing units were busted leading to seizure of around 25 lakh sticks of cigarettes along with 03 sets of cigarette manufacturing and packing machines. So far in the current Financial Year, DGGI has booked six (06) cases involving manufacture/supply of cigarettes and seized more than 10.07 crore sticks of cigarettes valued at over ₹ 160 crore , apart from machinery, packing material, raw material etc. Further total quantum of the fraudulently availed GST refunds detected is over ₹ 110 crore so far. **** KT/KMN
